questions.stem: What does the term transgenic specifically require?

options.text: Genetic material transferred from one species to a different species
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
That defines a GMO, not transgenic status.
Removal is not the defining transfer.
Conventional breeding involves no transfer.

questions.stem: Which statement about GMOs and transgenic organisms is correct?

options.explanation: Both depend on introduced DNA.

options.text: Every transgenic organism is a GMO, but not every GMO is transgenic
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Same-species edits are GMOs without being transgenic.
The species barrier separates them.

questions.stem: A plant is modified using DNA from the same plant species. What is it?

options.explanation: Its DNA was artificially altered, so it qualifies as a GMO.
Such modifications are routine.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.
No cross-species transfer occurred.

questions.stem: An animal receives a gene from a different species. Classify it.

options.text: GMO only, since animals cannot be transgenic
options.explanation: Animals clearly can be transgenic.
It satisfies both definitions.
Hybrid status is a different concept.

options.text: Transgenic, because DNA crossed between species
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: Why does exam phrasing about transgenic organisms insist on the species wording?

options.text: Because the transfer must be between different species for the term to apply
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Because species names are hard to spell
options.explanation: Spelling is not the issue.

options.text: Because any DNA change qualifies equally
options.explanation: Only cross-species change qualifies.
The barrier is the whole definition.

questions.stem: State what transgenic means in genetic engineering.
questions.modelAnswer: Transgenic means genetic material has been transferred from one species to a different species.

questions.stem: Name the broader category that every transgenic organism belongs to.
questions.modelAnswer: Every transgenic organism is a genetically modified organism, since its DNA was artificially altered.

questions.stem: Explain why a same-species gene insertion fails the transgenic definition.
questions.modelAnswer: The transgenic definition demands genetic material from a different species, so material from the organism's own species satisfies GMO status but never crosses the species barrier.

questions.stem: A farmer's maize carries a bacterial poison gene while a neighbour's maize carries an extra maize allele. Apply the definitions to classify both crops.
questions.modelAnswer: The bacterial-gene maize is transgenic because its added DNA came from another species, while the neighbour's extra allele is only a GMO since the DNA stayed within the same species.
